title: Coordinate differential expressions and principal symbols on complex type forms
statement: Use the real and complex fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. For $n\geq0$ let $V=\mathbf C^n$ with real coordinate vectors $e_j$ indexed by $\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\{0,1\}$. Let $F_a=\operatorname{Alt}_{\mathbf R}^a(V,\mathbf C)$. For integers $p,q$ define $F^{p,q}\subset F_{(p+q)_+}$ to be zero outside $0\leq p,q\leq n$; inside that range it consists of tensors $\tau$ satisfying $\sum_j\tau(v_1,\ldots,iv_j,\ldots,v_{p+q})=i(p-q)\tau(v_1,\ldots,v_{p+q})$. These are the coordinate fibres of the type spaces of [def-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-data]. For an open $U\subset V$ and natural numbers $a,b,k$, a smooth coordinate differential expression of order at most $k$ is a family of smooth complex-linear maps $A_{\ell,j}:U\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(F_a,F_b)$, where $0\leq\ell\leq k$ and $j$ is an ordered list of $\ell$ real coordinate directions. Its action is $Af(z)=\sum_{\ell=0}^k\sum_j A_{\ell,j}(z)D^\ell f(z)(e_{j_1},\ldots,e_{j_\ell})$, with the empty list giving the order-zero term. Its degree-$k$ principal symbol at a real covector $\xi\in V^*_{\mathbf R}$ is $\sigma_k(A)(z,\xi)=\sum_j(\prod_{t=1}^k\xi(e_{j_t}))A_{k,j}(z)$, without a factor of $i$. Let $M$ be a complex manifold modeled on $V$ and use the concrete spaces $A^{p,q}(M)$ and coordinate pullbacks of [def-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-data]. A complex-linear map on smooth forms has differential order at most $k$ from type $(p,q)$ to $(r,s)$ if it sends that source type into the target type and in every atlas chart has such a coordinate expression, whose action agrees with the map on every smooth source-type section. For a type endomorphism it is elliptic of order $k$ if in every chart one can choose such a representing expression whose degree-$k$ symbol is a bijection of $F^{p,q}$ for every point and every nonzero real covector. Real ellipticity means that the same symbol, restricted from complex scalars to real scalars, is a bijection on the underlying real type fibre.

source.place: Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §3.1 tensor types and §6.2 definition immediately preceding Lemma 6.4, printed p.23; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. The ordered-coordinate-list expansion is the usual multi-index expansion with repeated multi-indices collected.
